original_question: Do analogues of the two MMPP conjectures extend to general Cox processes under suitable regularity conditions? More specifically, for Cox processes satisfying appropriate regularity assumptions, must the squared coefficient of variation of the event-stationary inter-event time be at least 1 and must the time-stationary first inter-event time stochastically dominate the event-stationary first inter-event time?
target_in_paper: The draft is closest to the concluding open direction that suggests extending the two formal MMPP conjectures to Cox processes: in Section 3.1 the paper states Conjecture 3.8 (for an irreducible MMPP, c^2 >= 1) and Conjecture 3.9 (for an irreducible MMPP, T_1^pi >=_st T_1^alpha), and in Section 4 it adds that, since any Cox process can be approximated by an MMPP, one may formulate versions of these conjectures for Cox processes under suitable regularity conditions. ([cambridge.org](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/B037C27C281FB3B22AA591EEB0B5CF99/S1446181122000013a.pdf/stationary-markovian-arrival-processes-results-and-open-problems.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the exact pair of conjectural properties at issue—(III) c^2 >= 1 and (IV) T_1^pi >=_st T_1^alpha—and it also tracks the paper's closing suggestion that analogous statements might be sought for general Cox processes under suitable regularity conditions. ([cambridge.org](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/B037C27C281FB3B22AA591EEB0B5CF99/S1446181122000013a.pdf/stationary-markovian-arrival-processes-results-and-open-problems.pdf))
missing_details: The paper's formal conjectures are not stated for Cox processes but for irreducible MMPPs; the Cox-process version appears only as a brief concluding suggestion, so a paper-faithful rewrite should say this explicitly. ([cambridge.org](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/B037C27C281FB3B22AA591EEB0B5CF99/S1446181122000013a.pdf/stationary-markovian-arrival-processes-results-and-open-problems.pdf))

The ambient object should be specified as a simple nontransient point process on the line, since that is the general setting in which the paper defines and relates T_1^pi, T_1^alpha, and c^2. ([cambridge.org](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/B037C27C281FB3B22AA591EEB0B5CF99/S1446181122000013a.pdf/stationary-markovian-arrival-processes-results-and-open-problems.pdf))

T_1^pi and T_1^alpha need to be defined explicitly as the first interarrival times in the time-stationary and event-stationary versions, respectively. ([cambridge.org](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/B037C27C281FB3B22AA591EEB0B5CF99/S1446181122000013a.pdf/stationary-markovian-arrival-processes-results-and-open-problems.pdf))

The first inequality should be written using the paper's notation c^2 := Var(T_1^alpha)/E[T_1^alpha]^2, so one needs assumptions ensuring that at least the first two moments of T_1^alpha exist. ([cambridge.org](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/B037C27C281FB3B22AA591EEB0B5CF99/S1446181122000013a.pdf/stationary-markovian-arrival-processes-results-and-open-problems.pdf))

The stochastic-order clause should be stated in its full quantifier form, namely T_1^pi >=_st T_1^alpha, meaning the domination is required for all t >= 0. In the MAP setting the paper rewrites this as pi e^{Ct} 1 >= alpha e^{Ct} 1 for all t >= 0. ([cambridge.org](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/B037C27C281FB3B22AA591EEB0B5CF99/S1446181122000013a.pdf/stationary-markovian-arrival-processes-results-and-open-problems.pdf))

A nearby paper-critical reformulation is omitted: for any simple nontransient point process on the line, c^2 >= 1 is equivalent to E[T_1^pi] >= E[T_1^alpha] (Lemma 2.1). ([cambridge.org](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/B037C27C281FB3B22AA591EEB0B5CF99/S1446181122000013a.pdf/stationary-markovian-arrival-processes-results-and-open-problems.pdf))

No concrete 'suitable regularity conditions' for Cox processes are given in the paper itself, so a faithful rewrite should not pretend that the paper already fixes those hypotheses. ([cambridge.org](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/B037C27C281FB3B22AA591EEB0B5CF99/S1446181122000013a.pdf/stationary-markovian-arrival-processes-results-and-open-problems.pdf))
refined_question: Let N be a stationary simple nontransient Cox point process on R for which the time-stationary and event-stationary versions are both well defined, and assume E[(T_1^alpha)^2] < infinity so that c^2 := Var(T_1^alpha)/E[T_1^alpha]^2 is defined. If T_1^pi and T_1^alpha denote the first interarrival times in the time-stationary and event-stationary versions, respectively, do the Cox-process analogues of the two MMPP conjectures hold—namely, must c^2 >= 1 and must T_1^pi >=_st T_1^alpha? ([cambridge.org](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/B037C27C281FB3B22AA591EEB0B5CF99/S1446181122000013a.pdf/stationary-markovian-arrival-processes-results-and-open-problems.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: For the first assertion only, the paper proves that for any simple nontransient point process on the line, c^2 >= 1 is equivalent to E[T_1^pi] >= E[T_1^alpha]. So an equivalent reformulation of the first Cox-process analogue is to ask whether E[T_1^pi] >= E[T_1^alpha]. ([cambridge.org](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/B037C27C281FB3B22AA591EEB0B5CF99/S1446181122000013a.pdf/stationary-markovian-arrival-processes-results-and-open-problems.pdf))
justification: The draft is already pointed at the right open direction, but it needs the paper's exact scope and notation to become stand-alone. The paper formally conjectures the two MMPP statements in Section 3.1 and only then remarks in the conclusion that analogous Cox-process versions may be formulated; it does not itself supply the Cox regularity hypotheses. The nearby context that makes the question precise is the introduction's list of properties (III) and (IV), Proposition 2.2 defining T_1 via the time-stationary/event-stationary initializations, the formulas for c^2, and Lemma 2.1 showing the expectation reformulation of c^2 >= 1. That is why the refined question keeps the Cox extension but adds the minimal stand-alone setup rather than broadening beyond the paper. ([cambridge.org](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/B037C27C281FB3B22AA591EEB0B5CF99/S1446181122000013a.pdf/stationary-markovian-arrival-processes-results-and-open-problems.pdf))
